A.explanation: Horizontal is too small because the two rightward $x$-components are not both added, but the vertical $0.534\text{ N}$ is the correct upward minus downward difference.

B.explanation: Horizontal is too small and vertical $10.2\text{ N}$ adds $15.0\sin20.0^{\circ}$ and $6.00\cos40.0^{\circ}$ instead of subtracting opposite up and down components.

C.explanation: Horizontal adds $15.0\cos20.0^{\circ}$ and $6.00\sin40.0^{\circ}$ to give $18.0\text{ N}$, and vertical subtracts $6.00\cos40.0^{\circ}$ from $15.0\sin20.0^{\circ}$ to give $0.534\text{ N}$.

D.explanation: Horizontal $18.0\text{ N}$ correctly adds both rightward parts, but vertical $10.2\text{ N}$ wrongly adds the upward and downward parts instead of finding their difference.

hints: Notice the given angles are measured from different reference lines: $20.0^{\circ}$ from the horizontal for the $15.0\text{ N}$ force and $40.0^{\circ}$ from the vertical for the $6.00\text{ N}$ force.

Connect each angle to adjacent over hypotenuse: for the $15.0\text{ N}$ force use $\cos20.0^{\circ}$ for horizontal and $\sin20.0^{\circ}$ for vertical, and for the $6.00\text{ N}$ force use $\sin40.0^{\circ}$ for horizontal and $\cos40.0^{\circ}$ for vertical.

Next compare directions before adding: both horizontal parts point right so add them, but the $15.0\text{ N}$ vertical part points up while the $6.00\text{ N}$ vertical part points down so subtract to get the magnitude.
walkthrough: Resolve the $15.0\text{ N}$ force with $20.0^{\circ}$ above the horizontal. Horizontal is adjacent: $F_x1 = 15.0\cos20.0^{\circ}$, vertical is opposite: $F_y1 = 15.0\sin20.0^{\circ}$ upward.

Resolve the $6.00\text{ N}$ force with $40.0^{\circ}$ from the vertical toward the right. Horizontal is now opposite the angle: $F_x2 = 6.00\sin40.0^{\circ}$ to the right, vertical is adjacent: $F_y2 = 6.00\cos40.0^{\circ}$ downward.
Calculate the horizontal parts: $F_x1 = 15.0 \times 0.9397 = 14.1\text{ N}$ and $F_x2 = 6.00 \times 0.6428 = 3.86\text{ N}$. Both act right, so resultant magnitude is $14.1 + 3.86 = 18.0\text{ N}$.

Calculate the vertical parts: upward $F_y1 = 15.0 \times 0.3420 = 5.13\text{ N}$ and downward $F_y2 = 6.00 \times 0.7660 = 4.60\text{ N}$. They oppose, so resultant magnitude is $5.13 - 4.60 = 0.534\text{ N}$.
Pair $18.0\text{ N}$ horizontal with $0.534\text{ N}$ vertical. This is option C.
